newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 97 budget passes congress first reading.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 97 budget passes congress first reading.

text.p: Venezuela's proposed 1997 government budget for 7.83 trillion bolivars ($16.8 billion) passed a general first reading in the congressional house on Thursday, legislators said.

"There'll be a more ample discussion during the second reading when the government will have to truly reconcile spending and revenues," said Gustavo Tarre Briceno, President of the influential Congressional Finance Commission and member of opposition christian democrat party Copei. Following congress's okay, which would have to come before November 30, the bill would go onto further readings in the Senate.

This year's budget, a rolled-over 1995 budget subsequently plumped-up with supplementary credits, reached 5.3 trillion bolivars. Of that amount, 4.5 billion bolivars were deemed "ordinary revenues," compared with 6.5 trillion bolivars of ordinary revenues in the proposed 1997 budget.
"There are some doubts about the 1997 budget on the revenue side," said Tarre Briceno.
"In real terms they're almost the same as last year, which, as the sales tax has increased, as has the tax base, is somewhat contradictory," he added.
